references.text: Repeats the command to make holy garments for Aaron's sons, for glory and beauty, with the same purpose as for Aaron himself.
Describes the dressing of Aaron in the holy garments that were commanded in chapter 28.
Mentions the woven garments and the holy garments for the priest Aaron as part of the tabernacle equipment.
The fulfillment of the command—the holy garments were made for service in the sanctuary, for Aaron.
Confirmation that the woven garments for priestly service and the holy garments for Aaron were completed.
Moses dresses Aaron in the holy priestly garments as God had commanded.
The Lord clothes His priests with salvation, a spiritual parallel to the physical garments of glory and beauty.
Garments of salvation and a robe of righteousness for beauty use the same Hebrew root for beauty (תִפְאֶרֶת).
Regulations concerning the priests' garments in the future temple continue the principle of holy garments.
Refers to the high priest who is appointed to serve on behalf of people before God, with Aaron mentioned as a model.
Christ revealed in a long robe, like the high priest's attire, displays His priestly glory.
The bride's shining, pure linen represents the righteous deeds of the saints—a spiritual parallel to the priestly garments.
Complementary steps in the same ritual process: from the making of the garments to their use in the consecration.
Fulfillment of the command in 28:2 through the actual consecration of Aaron in holy garments.
The garments from 28:2 are the necessary prerequisite for the anointing and sanctification described here.
Reveals the enduring function of the garments from Exodus 28:2 as an inheritance for future priests.
Confirmation of completion: The command in Exodus 28:2 is fulfilled as holy garments for service.
The practical execution of the command in Exodus 28:2 through the dressing of Aaron.
